tutorial.stepWelcomeBody: Your household inventory — scan, organize, and find anything in seconds.
tutorial.stepScanBody: Scan any barcode or QR code. If it's already in your inventory, it opens instantly. If not, you can create an item or place right from the scan.
tutorial.stepOrganizeBody: Places can nest inside each other — a box in a shelf in a room. Move items between places, or scan a place's code to set an item's location.
tutorial.stepAskBody: Type or speak: “Where are the batteries?” The assistant searches your inventory and tells you the location.
tutorial.stepPrintBody: Print sheets of QR code labels for your items and places so you can tag physical things and scan them later.

help.title: Help
help.scanBody: Open the Scan tab and point at a barcode or QR code. A matched code opens the item or place. An unknown code lets you create a new item or place. From inside an item, tap “Scan to set location” and scan a place's code to move it there. From inside a place, tap “Scan to add” to move items in or nest another place. If a scan can't be applied, the reason appears over the camera and you can scan again straight away.
help.organizeBody: Places can be nested — a box inside a shelf inside a room. On an item, use the Location card to change its place or scan a new one. On a place, use the Location card to move it into another place. The places list shows where each place lives.
help.askBody: On the Ask screen, type or speak a question like “Where are the Christmas lights?” The assistant finds matching items and tells you their locations. Tap a result to open the item.
help.printBody: Go to Settings → Print codes. Select the items and places you want labels for, then tap Print / Share to generate a PDF. Only things that already have an app code are listed — give one a code from its own screen first. You can also run `npm run labels` on a computer to print blank label sheets to stick on things before they exist in the app.
help.codesBody: New items and places start with no code at all. When you want one, open it and either tap “Generate app code” for a printable StuffSearch QR, or “Scan to add a code” to attach a barcode or label that's already on the object. One thing can carry several codes, in any format.
help.tagsBody: Add tags like “return” or “fragile” to items and places, then tap a tag on the Items or Places tab to filter by it. Each item can also carry a value — tap ✨ Identify from photo to have the assistant estimate one from the picture, then correct the number yourself. The Items tab totals everything on screen.
